get.description: Liveness check. Touches no database or other dependency.

Readiness check: 200 when the database answers and is migrated, 503 otherwise.

Needs the service key: it queries the database, so it must not be an
open probe on a public URL. Liveness (`/health`) stays open.

``migrations`` compares the database's Alembic revision with this build's
head. Behind, or no ``alembic_version`` at all, answers 503 with status
``migrations_pending``: no deploy runs ``alembic upgrade head`` (ADR-011), and code
on an unmigrated schema fails every query on the changed tables. A revision this
build does not know counts as ahead (a newer build migrated) and is not pending.
Any other database error answers 503 ``unavailable`` with no ``migrations``.

Redis is deliberately not checked: rate limiting fails open, so a Redis blip
must not take the service out of rotation.

401.description: Invalid authentication, or a two-factor code is missing (code totp_required) or wrong (code totp_invalid)

503.description: Rate limiter unavailable, or the two-factor secret or key cannot be used (sign-in is refused)

get.description:
Who the session cookie belongs to, with revocation checked.

Unlike ``GET /session`` an unverified email is allowed (``email_verified`` says
which), and the per-user limit is the API one, so a server can call it on every
request. Callers that need a verified email check the flag themselves.

post.description:
Verify a Firebase ID token (signature, expiry, revocation) and echo its identity.

Identity only, never proof of a recent sign-in: there is no freshness check and
nothing is written (sign-in and refresh keep their own checks), and an unverified
email is returned with ``email_verified`` false for the caller to act on.

put.description:
Set a new password. The current password is proven by the fresh ``id_token``.

Firebase revokes the user's refresh tokens, which includes the caller's own session:
sign in again with the new password and call ``POST /v1/auth/session`` after a 200
(the re-auth ID token predates the revoke; unverified against live Firebase).

post.description:
Everything stored about the caller: profile, settings, memberships (with the
organisation's subscription), login history and notifications. Secrets, tokens and
other users' data are never included. Rate limited; each call is audit logged.

get.description:
The platform currency code (upper case, e.g. ``GBP``).

Answers ``GBP`` when the setting is missing or not a supported code. Sends
``Cache-Control: private, max-age=60`` and an ``ETag``.

Stripe unit amounts for the paid plans, in minor units.

A price that is not configured or cannot be read is ``null``; the caller falls back
to its default. Sends ``Cache-Control: private, max-age=300``.

Published offers that have not ended, with the total before paging.

``type`` may repeat. Without ``sort`` the newest come first.
A live offer. An ended offer answers 410 with ``expired: true`` and its title.

post.summary: Record an outbound click and return the destination
post.description: Write one click event for a live offer and return its affiliate destination.

Store a PENDING sign-up and email a confirmation link.

The answer is identical for a new address, a pending one, a confirmed one and an unsubscribed one, and
a confirmation is re-sent at most once an hour. Nothing says whether an email went out.
PENDING to CONFIRMED. A forged, expired, used or wrong-purpose token is the same 400.
Idempotent: unsubscribing twice succeeds twice. Used by the page and by one-click POSTs.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Sanitised JSON object, or null. Keys: `actor_role` (admin routes), `request_id` (admin and billing routes), `before`, `after` and `details` (changed fields; secret-looking keys and values are `[REDACTED]`). Billing rows carry `request_id` and, for plan changes and payment method changes only, `details`; checkout, cancel and resume rows have no `details`.
